discovery: Rydberg-blockade quantum simulation and computation with programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation and quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned the strong, long-range interaction between Rydberg atoms into a controllable resource. Saffman and Browaeys first demonstrated Rydberg blockade between two individually trapped atoms (2009) and the resulting entanglement and controlled-NOT gates. Lukin co-proposed the blockade mechanism for neutral-atom quantum logic. Browaeys and Lukin then developed defect-free, reconfigurable optical-tweezer arrays of hundreds of atoms. With them they realised quantum Ising and XY magnets, observed quantum phase transitions and many-body scars, and probed topological spin liquids. Most recently, Lukin's group with collaborators demonstrated logical qubits and error-corrected circuits on these arrays. The work opened a new field and is now one of the leading platforms for quantum simulation and computation. It shows how clean atomic physics can address central questions in condensed matter and quantum information.
